items.english: "You won't listen, will you." The young father gazed steadily at the small round arms and at the child's eyes with their long, rather dark lashes, moving without a pause, quick and knowing, as if wondering what was to be done, until presently, with a smile over his whole face, lightly pinching the child's round, thrust-out cheek with his finger, he felt under the table for a large bowl as if searching for it and put it into her hand.
notes: I take 彼女の手 as the mother's hand: he hands her the bowl, and in p8 she serves the rice from the pot into it and hands it to him. The text does not name her, so I keep the plain pronoun. For 怜悧に I follow the gloss sense of quick and knowing.

items.english: She served him rice from the pot, hot and newly cooked, with the white steam rising thickly. And her young large eyes too, full of a mother's gladness, watched the child, never still for an instant, lovely as a small bird. And as if she could not bear it, murmuring to herself, "Whatever is the matter with this child," looking as if the child were dear beyond all help, she said firmly, "Baby," but the smile overflowed from her face, and she looked at the man's face as if asking for help. And the three of them, as if they had forgotten everything, smiled at one another as if wondering what to do for the child. And for the sake of the child they set to their meal with a warm bustle and with a smile and gladness overflowing of itself. In the clattering noise, too, they did not hear the sound of the rain and wind.
notes: For 坊や I use Baby throughout for the girl child, keeping the call plain and affectionate without marking sex; the period generic use for a stated girl is left for the margin. I keep smile overflowed and warm bustle in the same plain words as elsewhere, and sound of the rain and wind literal so the hearing arc stays sound.

items.english: The young father kept his large red hand spread busily over the table. And holding back the smile the child helplessly brought welling up, he steadied the child and put a little food into the small red mouth. In the gaps, hastily opening his own large mouth, he pushed rice into it.
notes: I keep the feeding physical and in snatches: his hand spread to guard, the child's mouth fed, his own mouth filled in the gaps, without smoothing into one tidy action.

data.say: Drafted the noisy supper at the table in the same plain voice, keeping smiles, bustle, and feeding literal.
